summary: Groups can now be kept in separate memory workspaces: what Nora remembers about people in one workspace's groups is built only from those groups, and within a workspace each group's recall draws on that group's own chats.
details: policy.toml can put each group (unit) in a workspace with a [units] table, and identity.toml says which Honcho workspace each workspace's memories live in; with no [units] table everything works exactly as before.
A group may have at most one room per platform; a policy that gives a group two rooms on the same platform now refuses to start.
Memory reads for a room or group now use that group's own Honcho scope, and anything Nora is asked to remember is written where those reads look.
New operator command `nora memory backfill --unit <unit>` replays a group's recorded messages into its own workspace (a dry run unless --apply).
limitations: Right after a group moves into a scope, recall starts from the facts people stated directly; deeper conclusions come back as Honcho re-derives them.
Facts saved with `remember` before this change are not in any group's scope, so a group's recall no longer sees them.
Once [units] is set, the web portal's memory page shows nothing until someone decides which workspace it should show for a person in several.
